   Life needs energy



⬣   Recall that living organisms are built of complex
    structures


⬣   Building complex structures that are low in entropy
    is only possible when energy is spent in the process


⬣   The ultimate source of this energy on Earth is the
    sunlight

pages.text:
Dr. Osama Essawi 2025

               Life needs energy


  ⬣    Two large groups of living organisms based on carbon source

-Autotrophs use atmospheric CO2 to construct carbon-containing
               biomolecules
-Heterotrophs obtain carbon from complex organic molecules like glucose

  ⬣    Autotrophs can be photosynthetic, using sunlight for energy, while
       heterotrophs rely on organic nutrients

  ⬣    Autotrophs and heterotrophs exist in an interdependent cycle, exchanging
       carbon, oxygen, and water

  ⬣    Solar energy is the driving force behind the global cycling of carbon,
       oxygen, and nitrogen

      Metabolism is the sum of all
     chemical reactions in the cell


●   Series of related reactions form metabolic pathways

●   Some pathways are primarily energy-producing

pages.text:
Dr. Osama Essawi 2025
              Energy Laws -                Laws of Thermodynamics


●   The first law of thermodynamics is the principle of the
    conservation of energy: for any physical or chemical
    change, the total amount of energy in the universe
    remains constant; energy may        change form or it may be
    transported from one region to another, but it         cannot be
    created or destroyed.

●   The second law of thermodynamics, states that the
    universe always tends toward increasing disorder: in all
    natural processes, the entropy of the universe increases.

concepts.label: First law
concepts.detail: Total energy in the universe remains constant during physical or chemical change. Energy changes form or location but cannot be created or destroyed.
concepts.rationale: Source explicitly teaches this relationship or distinction.

concepts.label: Second law
concepts.detail: The slide states that the entropy of the universe increases in all natural processes.
concepts.rationale: Source explicitly teaches this relationship or distinction.

pages.title: Thermodynamic quantities describing energy changes
pages.visualReviewBy: Codex chapter writer (second-agent content review still pending)
pages.visualReviewNotes: Inspected rendered page in a contact sheet; image-only content was checked at full-page resolution where needed. No printed slide number is visible.
pages.text:
Dr. Osama Essawi 2025
               Thermodynamic quantities describing energy changes



⬣    Free energy (ΔG) is the energy that can perform work during a reaction.
            - Exergonic reactions release free energy (ΔG < 0)
            - Endergonic reactions gain free energy (ΔG > 0).

⬣    Enthalpy (ΔH) is the heat content of the reacting system.
            - Exothermic reactions release heat (ΔH < 0)
            - Endothermic reactions absorb heat (ΔH > 0).

⬣    Entropy (ΔS) is a measure of randomness or disorder in a system. Reactions
     with a gain in entropy involve more disordered products.

⬣    The relationship between ΔG, ΔH, and ΔS is given by the equation
                                   ΔG = ΔH –      TΔS
pages.visualDetails: Graph axes: potential energy of molecules versus progress of reaction. Exergonic graph has higher reactant than product energy and shows energy output; endergonic graph has higher product than reactant energy and shows energy input.

concepts.label: Free energy and reaction sign
concepts.detail: Free energy ΔG is energy capable of performing work. Exergonic reactions release free energy (ΔG < 0); endergonic reactions gain free energy (ΔG > 0).
concepts.rationale: Source explicitly teaches this relationship or distinction.

concepts.label: Enthalpy and heat sign
concepts.detail: Enthalpy ΔH is the heat content of the reacting system. Exothermic reactions release heat (ΔH < 0); endothermic reactions absorb heat (ΔH > 0).
concepts.rationale: Source explicitly teaches this relationship or distinction.

concepts.label: Entropy
concepts.detail: Entropy ΔS measures randomness/disorder. Gain of entropy corresponds to more disordered products.
concepts.rationale: Source explicitly teaches this relationship or distinction.

concepts.label: Gibbs energy equation
concepts.detail: ΔG = ΔH − TΔS.
concepts.rationale: Source explicitly teaches this relationship or distinction.

Dr. Osama Essawi 2025

     Gibbs free energy and equilibrium constan                                                       t

⬣    Equilibrium constant (Keq) is defined by the concentrations of reactants and products at equilibrium in
     a general reaction







⬣    Standard free-energy change ΔG′°       is the force driving a system toward equilibrium under standard
     conditions of temperature, pressure, and initial concentrations.

⬣    The relationship between     ΔG′°  and K′ eq  can be represented by the equation:
                                              ΔG′°    = −RT lnK′eq

pages.title: Energetics of Some Chemical Reactions
pages.visualReviewBy: Codex chapter writer (second-agent content review still pending)
pages.visualReviewNotes: Inspected rendered page in a contact sheet; image-only content was checked at full-page resolution where needed. No printed slide number is visible.
pages.text:
Dr. Osama Essawi 2025

       Energetics of Some Chemical Reactions



⬣    Hydrolysis reactions tend to be strongly favorable(spontaneous)

⬣    Isomerization reactions have smaller free-energy changes
             -Isomerization between enantiomers: ΔG′°            = 0

⬣    Complete oxidation of reduced compounds is strongly favorable

             -This is how chemotrophs       obtain most of their energy
             - In biochemistry, the oxidation of reduced fuels with O2 is stepwise and controlled
             -Recall that being thermodynamically favorable is not the same as being kinetically rapid

     More examples can be found in TABLE 13-4Standard Free-Energy Changes of Some Chemical Reactions
pages.visualDetails: Footer refers to TABLE 13-4 Standard Free-Energy Changes of Some Chemical Reactions. The actual table is not reproduced on this slide and is not a supplied source.

concepts.label: Hydrolysis energetics
concepts.detail: Hydrolysis reactions tend to be strongly favorable/spontaneous.
concepts.rationale: Source explicitly teaches this relationship or distinction.

concepts.label: Isomerization energetics
concepts.detail: Isomerizations have smaller free-energy changes; isomerization between enantiomers has ΔG′° = 0.
concepts.rationale: Source explicitly teaches this relationship or distinction.

concepts.label: Favorable oxidation versus reaction rate
concepts.detail: Complete oxidation of reduced compounds is strongly favorable; chemotrophs obtain much of their energy this way. Oxidation with O2 is stepwise and controlled. Thermodynamically favorable does not mean kinetically rapid.
concepts.rationale: Source explicitly teaches this relationship or distinction.

Dr. Osama Essawi 2025

       Chemical Reactivity



⬣   Most of the reactions in living cells fall into one of five general categories:
          1) Reactions that make or break carbon–carbon bonds
          2) Internal rearrangements, isomerizations, and eliminations
          3) Free-radical reactions
          4) Group transfers
          5) Oxidation-reductions

concepts.detail: The listed categories are making/breaking C–C bonds; internal rearrangements/isomerizations/eliminations; free-radical reactions; group transfers; oxidation-reductions. This is a list, not a temporal sequence.
concepts.rationale: Source explicitly teaches this relationship or distinction.

Dr. Osama Essawi 2025
Homolytic             vs. Heterolytic
Cleavage


 ⬣    Covalent bonds can be broken in two ways

 ⬣    Homolytic   cleavage is very rare

 ⬣    Heterolytic  cleavage is common, but the products are
      highly unstable and this dictates the chemistry that
      occurs
pages.visualDetails: Aligned reaction diagrams label carbon radical, H atom, carbon radicals, carbanion, proton, carbocation and hydride. Dots indicate radical electrons; pairs/charges distinguish ionic products. This is a comparison diagram rather than a printed data table.

concepts.detail: Homolytic C–H cleavage produces carbon radical + H atom; homolytic C–C cleavage produces carbon radicals. Heterolytic C–H cleavage can give carbanion + proton or carbocation + hydride; heterolytic C–C cleavage gives carbanion + carbocation.
concepts.rationale: Source explicitly teaches this relationship or distinction.

concepts.label: Relative cleavage frequency
concepts.detail: Homolytic cleavage is described as very rare; heterolytic cleavage is common, with highly unstable products that dictate subsequent chemistry.
concepts.rationale: Source explicitly teaches this relationship or distinction.

Dr. Osama Essawi 2025
                Phosphoryl Transfer from ATP



⬣   Phosphoryl group transfers are significant in
    metabolic pathways.
⬣   Inorganic orthophosphate (Pi) and inorganic
    pyrophosphate (PPi) are common leaving
    groups in nucleophilic substitution reactions.
⬣   Nucleophilic substitutions are facilitated by
    attaching a phosphoryl group to a poor leaving
    groups, such as hydroxyl (OH).
⬣   In metabolic reactions, a phosphoryl group is
    often transferred from ATP to form a
    phosphate ester.

Dr. Osama Essawi 2025
 Hydrolysis of ATP is highly favorable under
                standard conditions




⬣ Better charge separation in products

⬣ More favorable resonance stabilization
  of products

⬣ Energy is released from ATP through
  the loss of phosphate groups

Body text says energy is released through loss of phosphate groups; this is preserved as a description of the overall hydrolysis process, not an added claim that bond cleavage alone releases energy.

concepts.label: ATP hydrolysis standard energy

                    Phosphoenolpyruvate (PEP) hydrolysis

Dr. Osama Essawi 2025
               ATP hydrolysis in two steps


⬣    ATP participates covalently in enzyme-catalyzed
     reactions, contributing free energy to the process.


⬣    In the first step part of the ATP molecule, such as a
     phosphoryl or pyrophosphoryl         group is transferred
     to a substrate or an amino acid residue in an
     enzyme.

⬣    This covalent attachment raises the free-energy
     content of the substrate or enzyme, activating it.

     first step is displaced, generating Pi, Ppi     as the
     leaving group.

pages.text:
Dr. Osama Essawi 2025

                  ATP as Energy Source in Metabolism

⬣    Intermediate Energy Release:

              -While compounds like PEP release more energy, ATP's intermediate release is suitable for cellular processes.
              -Releasing too much energy at once could be inefficient or harmful.

⬣    Regulation:

              -Controlled ATP hydrolysis ensures a managed and regulated energy release.
              -Tuning energy release is crucial for specific cellular activities.

⬣    Economic Considerations:

              -ATP synthesis and hydrolysis are efficiently coupled to metabolic pathways.
              -The cost of ATP synthesis and usage is reasonable, making it an economical choice for cells               .

⬣    Buffering Capacity:

              -ATP is present in high concentrations, providing a readily available energy reservoir.

⬣   Dehydrogenations are common biological oxidations where a
    compound loses two electrons and two hydrogen ions.

⬣   Oxidation reactions generally release energy, and most living cells
    obtain energy by oxidizing metabolic fuels like carbohydrates or
    fats.

                  How Enzymes Work

⬣    Catalysis of the Reaction:

            - Enzymes stabilize the transition state, lowering
            activation energy.
            - This accelerates specific biochemical reactions.

            - Catalyzed reactions result in product formation.
            - Products are released, and enzymes remain unchanged.
            - Enzymes are available for reuse, catalyzing multiple
            reactions.
